findings.question: q-biology-cellular-respiration-and-fermentation-0006
findings.quote: Both pathways make ATP without oxygen. This puts oxygen into fermentation. Check whether either pathway uses oxygen as its final acceptor.
findings.problem: The note identifies the oxygen error and gives a check, but never explains why the oxygen-requiring fermentation choice might look right. For example, a student may transfer the familiar oxygen requirement of aerobic respiration to fermentation.
findings.fix: Add that the student may be applying the oxygen requirement of aerobic respiration to fermentation.

findings.question: q-biology-cellular-respiration-and-fermentation-0006
findings.quote: Some fermentation forms carbon dioxide, as in yeast. The products do not separate the two pathways. Check which feature all anaerobic respiration shares.
findings.problem: The note corrects the product-based distinction and gives a check, but omits why this choice might look right. For example, a student who remembers muscle fermentation may assume all fermentation produces lactate.
findings.fix: Explain that remembering muscle fermentation can lead a student to treat lactate as the product of every kind of fermentation.
